en_pages.text: (But actually, there's something else playing on my mind, as it happens...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Oh! There's someone curled up in a ball in the back corner, look!
What's his name again? Professor Albert Harebrayne, wasn't it?
...Um, excuse me! Professor Harebrayne!
Who are you?
I'm Ryunosuke Naruhodo. I'm a defence lawyer.
Agh! (Was it something I said?!)
A, a lawyer, you say?
W-W-W-Would you be here... a-a-a-about the experiment?
ARE YOU GOING TO DEFEND MY HYPOTHESIS?!
Your...hypothesis? Sorry, I don't–
Yesterday's demonstration!
That demonstration was... That magnificent demonstration was...
It was an out-and-out success! By anyone's calculations!
B-B-B-But despite that...
...no one listens! No lawyer believes in the science! When it's explained, they all leave...at high velocity!
(Now's probably not a good time to mention that your zeal made my concentration leave for a while, too...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Ugh... The showgrounds are a little too big for my liking...
We've been walking around in dense crowds for two hours now, and I've felt myself swooning three times.
There are a lot of people, aren't there? I've almost been trodden on three times, too!
...Be careful, won't you, Iris? Don't let go of my hand.
(We've finally made it through the throngs though, by the look of it.)
(Here we are underneath the public experimentation stage where the explosion happened yesterday.)
(What's that...?)
(I can hear voices from up on the stage. It sounds like an argument...)
Right, I've had it with you this time! I'm warnin' you, I'll arrest you in a minute!
Oh yeah? Go on then, 'Spector, give it a shot! You ain't got no evidence, an' you know it!
(Wait... I know those voices.)
You've got a cheeky little mouth on you, young lady! But a night in the cells will teach you some manners!
Just try it, I dare ya! If ya want that bag o' chips rammed down yer throat!
Yoo-hoo! Gregsy! What are you doing up there?
AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH! It's you! Here! You're here! Here you are! You! Here!
How are you, Your Ladyship? I do hope you're well, Your Ladyship?
(...Does that make her three times a lady?)
I'm not well at all. It's far too busy everywhere.
I wanted to ride in a balloon, but there was a three-hour queue.
Unbelievable! I'll go an' have a word for you at once, Your Ladyship!
You'll be flyin' as high as a kite in no time once I pull some strings for you!
Tobias Gregson, an inspector at Scotland Yard.
Until recently, he was suspended from duty, but it would appear he's back in action now.
He's actually quite well known, appearing as he does in ‘The Adventures of Herlock Sholmes’.
And for that reason, he can't say a word wrong to the stories' author, Iris.
(But there are limits, surely... Or there should be!)
Watch it, sunshine!
What gives, then? Don't tell me you're on this case?
Yes, I'm acting for the defence.
So we're here to investigate!
Hmmm... Dear me, that's the situation, is it?
(Is it really that troubling?)
Tsk. A measly five bob? Is that all ya got?
Yer a lawyer, ain't ya? Ya could stand to carry a bit more copper around in yer pockets, Mr Narra-'Oddo!
Wha...? Hey! That's my last bit of spending money, that is!
Ya can 'ave it back, but I'll 'ave to charge ya for all the bother. Three bob.
This is Gina Lestrade, a pickpocket, or ‘diver’, born and bred in the East End of London.
In the case that led to my own suspension six months ago...
...this is the young girl I was defending in court.
Wot's yer problem, eh, 'Oddo?!
‘Diver’? Pickpocket? Wot's wiv all the name-callin'?
You wanna bag o' chips rammed down yer throat an' all, do ya?
I, I thought you were proud to be a diver, Gina?
You were just arguing with Inspector Gregson about it, weren't you?
I assumed you'd been up to your usual tricks here at the showground.
That ain't no way to talk to a lady, 'Oddo. 'Alf a year's a long time. People can change.
I'm an apprentice now. Learnin' to be a Scotland Yard detective.
So you'll 'ave to call me wot everyone else does: It's Inspector Lestrade now!
Inspector?! (That badge is homemade, surely...)
The ‘inspector’ part isn't entirely accurate. No one calls her that.
For what it's worth, anyway. Investigatin' is off the cards for all of us.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Right, well, I'll be back up top. You hold the fort down here, alright?
(This raises a LOT of questions!)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Right, are you done here, Mr Naruhodo?
That lot are here now.
The Forensic Investigation Team. They'll be givin' me the heave-ho in a minute, too.
Oh dear. Poor Gregsy.
Here! Have another cup of my special blend to cheer you up!
*Glug* *Glug glug glug*
Aaah! That hit the spot! Yup, hits it every time!
(Well, at least I've seen the scene with my own eyes.)
(It looks like this is as far as we're going to get with our investigations here at least...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Hurley might know something, mightn't he?
...! About what happened to Lord van Zieks, you mean?
(Because it sounds like something very significant occurred after he graduated from university.)
(Something that completely changed his life.)
Maybe, but I have no idea where to find Mr Sholmes at the moment.
He's in the middle of some big case, isn't he?
Here, this is what you need!
What's this? (Some kind of entrance ticket?)
‘Madame Tusspells’? Is this supposed to mean something to me?
You don't know it?!
It's the most popular attraction in London at the moment!
It's very close to Baker Street, actually. We could go now, if you like?
No no, we don't have time for visiting attractions today, Iris. We have a big trial tomorrow!
But that's where Hurley is.
What? At, at this popular London attraction?
How is it that you know where he is?
Hurley told me. But he told me to keep it a secret from you, Runo.
(I don't see how it could be related to the case we're investigating here, but then...)
(...stranger things have happened. And when they happen, Mr Sholmes is usually at the heart of them.)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I was sure that you'd know, Hurley.
You said there was something going on here in this exhibit hall before. That something was afoot.
And that you believed it was related to what I wanted to ask you about.
Um, Mr Sholmes...? (He's suddenly clammed up.)
Well, it seems we've reached the unavoida–
Oh! Ah...hello. (Where did she appear from?)
(And what's she wearing? Could she look any more mysterious?)
I hope...you are appreciating my museum?
Sorry? Have we...?
Mr Sholmes, do you know this–
My apologies. I am Esmeralda Tusspells. This is my museum of waxwork.
Wha... You... You're THE Madame Tusspells?
Bien sûr. Though only twenty-six years young, I might add.
...Is that significant somehow?
I'm a ‘madame’ in name only. It adds a certain...je ne sais quoi.
Firstly, I must apologise for my waxworks. Or rather, one waxwork in particular.
(That'll be Mr Sholmes, then.)
I was led to believe he was a great detective, but he seems...unable to settle.
Next time you move from your designated exhibit...there WILL be toil and trouble.
She sounds deadly serious.
(That's a problem.)
(How am I supposed to ask Mr Sholmes about Lord van Zieks now?)
Let's not forget what Hurley said before.
About something being afoot right here in the museum, I mean.
Yes, I know, but...
I'm so curious! I want to know what's happening here!
(Haven't we got enough on our plate already?)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I think I'd rather have two hundred pounds in my pocket.
Exactly. You could buy one of those brand new types of steam carriage!
That's what I'd spend it on if I had it, no question.
Ooh, I'd buy all the herbs in the world!
(There must be another explanation for the money... We need to keep looking.)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: L-Look at this!
He's, he's not tapping his foot consciously, then? So you mean...
...It must be a twitch!
Never mind that! The point is, waxworks don't tap their feet!
(And look at his arm, too...)
(We've seen a scarf like that somewhere else around here, haven't we?)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: He's a waxwork being sold for thruppence. It really couldn't be more obvious!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: À vos ordres ! It was murder, plain and simple. Anyone could state that with complete certainty.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: AAAAAAAAAH! Yes! Yes, that's right! Bien sûr !
(Well done, Docteur ! That was a great counter-argument!)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: (Alright. Time to tighten the screws here...)
If the prosecution is unable to explain this inconsistency in its argument...
...we can only conclude that the testimony given in support cannot be relied upon!
(Lord van Zieks is stumped!)
...Do you have something to say, witness?
Yes...I knew it...
It bears out... The equations hold...
Mr Naruhodo! ...DON'T WORRY!
Without delving into the details, there is no inconsistency!
Even if Andrew had been lodged in Mr Asman's chest...
...my trusty tool wouldn't have moved. Andrew remaining on the stage is consistent with my calculations!
It would seem your illusions have been...shattered. Clearly we should hear the accused's explanation.
...Or should I say, this brilliant scientist's explanation?
(Just when I'd found an inconsistency in the prosecution's argument...)
Very well! The defendant will testify again.
Provide us with the scientific explanation as to why the inconsistency asserted by the defence fails to hold!
In the name of Apollo, I will, My Lord!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: My only interest lies in upholding my hypothesis! I'm a scientist, after all!
(Is he working for us or against us? It's very hard to tell...)
Let's see how you cross-examine this testimony, my Nipponese friend.
Yes, fire away, Mr Naruhodo!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: ...A year ago now, a small provincial science journal published a little paper about my work.
That's a scientific journal? Good gracious, I should need new spectacles!
I might have had an extraordinary hypothesis and great promise, but at the time, I had no money.
I, I had to eat tiny little meals at a tiny little café and drink watered-down water out of a tiny little glass...
But...Mr Asman read the paper and came to visit me at my tiny little laboratory!
And offered you money to help fund your work?
Exactly! That's exactly what happened!
I handled the theoretical side of things, and Mr Asman provided me with an engineer for the practical.
...And the three of us produced that fantastic machine together!
The machine that you brought to the Great Exhibition to demonstrate.
We, we had to apply to the government for some sort of inspection to be allowed to exhibit, I think.
I didn't understand all that side of things. Mr Asman took care of all of it.
He was a wonderful man! Really, I owe him everything.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: My feeling is that the machine requires a thorough examination.
But what about this ‘special dispensation’ that's been mentioned? Oh gosh...this is all too much.
If it's determined that the machine itself was the murder weapon, I think you'll find that act won't apply.
Of course it was the murder weapon! Anyone can see that, as plain as day!
So we're all in agreement, are we? That the machine should be stripped?
...! (If, if I don't do something, they'll...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: But even so...
Even so, what?
Going to such trouble and expense to create a fake machine to display in public...
He would have absolutely no reason to do such a thing!
He had an obvious reason to do exactly that.
For the research grant money.
If the government was foolish enough to have deemed the man's ridiculous notion plausible...
...he and his conspirators would have received a handsome sum indeed.
What would be the value of such a grant? Ten pounds?
You're an order of magnitude out, madam. Five hundred pounds a YEAR!
Ooh arrrrrr! Ya could live 'andsome on that much for years!
The Society's noticed an increase in bogus public demonstrations in the field of science recently.
And plenty of scientists arguing with each other to get the largest slice of the funding cake.
People's greed is plenty motive enough for murder, I assure you!
No no no! I haven't deceived anyone! Least of all the government!
My hypothesis is sound! The science is sound! Please, you must believe me!
No matter how unbelievable this hypothesis may seem to you, ladies and gentlemen...
...the fact remains that the victim was transported instantly to the Crystal Tower.
Which means that the experiment...was a success.
...the only person who could possibly have committed this murder...is the accused!
(Where is this heading? I have no idea...)
My Lord, if I may...?
Yes, Lord van Zieks?
The prosecution would like to summon new witnesses to the stand.
New witnesses? What would be the nature of their involvement?
They were spectators of the demonstration at the exhibition. Who were occupying special seats.
Very well, the court grants the prosecution's request.
I should very much like to hear from eyewitnesses to the incident.
The prosecution's stance is clear. This experiment was no postiche.
The accused killed the financier victim there on the public stage, before the very eyes of the spectators.
Now, my learned friend...
It's time for you to make your own stance clear.
(There's clearly a flaw in the professor's hypothesis. I can definitely see that.)
(But where does that leave me...?)
We shall take a short recess now.
During which time, the prosecution will prepare its new witnesses to take the stand.
...As you wish, My Lord.
Good. In that case, court is adjourned for twenty minutes.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: M-Mr Naruhodo...
...what on earth were you playing at just now? Or rather...
...WHAT ON EARTH WERE YOU PLAYING AT ALL ALONG?!
MY HYPOTHESIS! MY AMAZING HYPOTHESIS! You've been picking holes in it from the start!
Ah, sorry about that.
But you promised me!
You, you said you'd prove that dratted explosion was an accident, not murder.
You said you'd keep my precious invention from falling into anyone else's hands!
But all you've done so far is try to undermine me!
......... Yes, I did make you a promise, you're right.
I said that I'd believe in you and fight for your freedom to the very end.
But I also told you I was no scientist. I don't understand your hypothesis.
The fact is, there's an undeniable flaw in your logic, isn't there?
Ah! But! If I just run through some equations... Yes, you see! It's because my work is incomplete!
Perhaps it is. Nevertheless...a man died as a consequence, didn't he?
Oh. OOOOOOOOOH NOOOOOOOOO!
You're right. You're so right. It's all my fault...
And I have no right to blame you for my failures.
I'm a disaster! Not just as a scientist...but as a human being!
Well...that might be a little over the top.
And while we're on the subject...
...wh-what about Barok? He's being awful!
Claiming his old university friend to be a murderer, you mean?
He's a disaster! Not just as a prosecutor...but as a human being!
Oh! But no! Wait! He's the Reaper, isn't he? Perhaps he's not classified as Homo sapiens any more...?
(...Glad that's cleared up...)
......... Can I double-check something with you?
The machine and demonstration you prepared... They were based entirely on your hypothesis, I presume?
There was no...trickery involved?
I drew the plans for the machine with my very own hands.
Every line was painstakingly drawn with the firm belief that science is the only future.
So yes, it's true that my hypothesis hasn't reach maturity yet, but please, Mr Naruhodo...you must believe in it.
......... Alright, Professor, I understand.
The prosecution's witnesses are ready to take the stand. Court is about to be in session again.
Make your way into the courtroom, please!
(It all hinges on that demonstration.)
(If the professor's hypothesis is sound as he claims...)
(...it leaves him as the only person who could possibly have killed the victim.)
(But on the other hand, Mr Sholmes was adamant...)
A practical implementation, such as was attempted by the professor at the Great Exhibition, is quite impossible.
(So really, what should I be trying to prove here?)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: It was an incidente terribile. I am only grateful that my balloons were not damaged.
There's this huge bang from the stage, and then the next second, another bang in the sky beside us.
And from amid ze smoke...a cage appeared out of nowhere!
The cage, it fell from the sky like a stone. And crashed into the Crystal Tower!
I didn't get a good look inside the cage, but no one went near it after it crashed into the tower.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Eh, no, in reality I did not. I saw after it hit the tower.
There was a grande confusione around the stage. I ran to see what had happened.
I was terrorised by the idea that one of my balloons had crashed!
(I suppose they are his livelihood...)
But when I looked up to the sky, all my precious balloons were still there!
I saw it, though. I saw it slam into the tower! After all, I am a detective now!
Then tell us what you saw...Inspector Lestrade.
That's wot I like to 'ear!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Eh? Use yer 'ead, 'Oddo! 'Ow could it 'ave been me? I was up in a balloon, weren't I?
So cos I weren't available, it was the boss who 'ad to leg it over there.
'E was gettin' shoved an' kicked all over by the panickin' spectators as 'e tried to seal off the scene.
It was a real sight to behold, I can tell ya! Amazin'!
(Poor Inspector Gregson...)
So anyway, I couldn't see the cage that well cos of all the smoke.
And I didn't really wanna see, to be honest. I was scared out me wits...
Keep it together, Inspector...

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond Ormstein.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: (But what if it was actually some kind of switch-around trick instead?)
(That would mean that the victim was never actually on the stage in the first place.)
(The two explosions would have thrown everyone watching into a panic for sure.)
(I think I need to find out more about what exactly people saw at the time...)

en_pages.text: Mr Lune, in your testimony...
...you said that all three of the balloons you had operating at the time were undamaged.
Si. That is correct. If they had been caught in the esplosiones, it would have been terribile.
I wonder...if you might know what this is?
Ah...I think it may be...
Si, part of a balloon. A burnt piece of the fabric of the envelope.
Sorry? The envelope?
Pardon. That is the large, round part of the balloon which becomes filled with hot air.
It is made from very thick fabric lined with rubber. You do not want it to rip when you are in the sky.
(Just as I thought...)
This piece of cloth was found near the experimentation stage. In other words, as Master Gotts testified...
...a green balloon did indeed explode that day.
If all the balloons in the sky above the experimentation stage belonged to you, Mr Lune...
...then your statement that they were all undamaged clearly contradicts the evidence!
If a balloon exploded that day, why didn't the man say so?
Maybe everyone on board was killed...
Oh no! Having just spent ten whole pounds for the experience?! How awful!
Seems to me like those things crash fifty percent of the time anyway...

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: All three of my balloons were carrying passengers. If they fell to the ground in an esplosione, what a catastrofe!
But ya can't get away from the fact that a burnt-up bit o' cloth was found at the scene, can ya?
The coppers at the Yard reckoned it was prob'ly some debris thrown from the explosion on the stage.
This stupido ragazzo is mistaken! My balloons have the red and blue zigzag stripes anyway!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: It's Prince Wilhelm Gottsreich Sigismond Ormstein.
...Your royal blood will not help you here, ragazzo.
Si, it is a balloon! But there is nothing more you can see from this black-and-white photograph!
Just look on my head! THAT is a Balthazar Lune balloon! The best in the business!
Let's try not to get over-inflated...
The point is this! Here we have clear photographic proof that in the sky above the experimentation stage...
...there may very well have been a balloon operated by somebody other than you, Mr Lune!
Who was it?! I want to know! Who was this mongrel with no respect for the boundaries?!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: It's time for definitives now. So tell the court...

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: It's clear that you drew the plans for the experiment, but you didn't actually build it.
It's quite conceivable that you were duped, Professor. If you'll just let me, I can prove–
I'll cooperate. I'll do whatever you say. I swear it.
So, so please...
...ensure the Special Dispensation for Scientific Equipment Act is adhered to and protect my creation!
...Pray forgive the discourtesy of filling my hallowed chalice at this critical juncture...
Here's to my learned Nipponese friend...
...and his upcoming attempt to clarify the defence's position in the light of the accused's confession.
Do you intend to formally assert that the experiment was nothing more than a conjuring trick?
Because the moment you do...
...the Special Dispensation for Scientific Equipment Act that protects the professor's invention will cease to apply.
The prosecution will then demand a rigorous examination of the machinery involved in order to establish the truth.
However...if you acknowledge that the machine is genuine and instrumental in the victim's murder...
...any chance of investigating will be crushed...and the confidentiality of the professor's hypothesis preserved.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I'm...I'm...I'm... I'm so sorry!
I was wrong! You were right! I tricked you! You trusted me! I dragged you...into my mess!
Oh h-how did it ever come to this...?
I'M SOOO SOOO SOOO SOOORRY!
Did you really have no idea, Professor?
About what Mr Drebber was really up to, I mean? About what he was really constructing.
That machine was the embodiment of my hypothesis! Of all my hopes and dreams!
I had complete faith in it!
Alright. In that case, I won't say any more.
Now, sadly the murder accusation against you still stands.
So we must do as much investigation as we can before the trial resumes tomorrow.
Well, thank you for doing so much for me!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: It would be foolish to ignore the skylight when it's directly adjacent to the footprints there.
Somehow or other, Mr Drebber clearly ‘landed’ on the ceiling and escaped that way.
Personally, I hold with my theory that he had very powerful springs in the soles of his shoes!
Mr Naruhodo, with that answer you haven't righted my reasoning in any way.
Oh...yes, that's true.
As a logician, you will never surpass me. The science of deduction and analysis requires long and patient study.
I'm several steps ahead of you. And your attempts to correct me serve only to highlight your deficiencies.
Ugh...this is what you get for agreeing with someone?

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: The reason there are footprints on the ceiling...is because of the nearby chaussure toute proche !
The reason there are footprints on the ceiling...is because of the nearby chaussure toute proche !
And on closer inspection, there are clearly footprints all over the balloon as well.
In other words, the aim was never the skylight at all, but the balloon.
But...for what purpose ?
A green balloon... Hmmm, that seems somewhat familiar data.
And inside the green balloon that Master Gotts claims he saw above the stage when the incident occurred...
You, you mean to say... ?
If we assume the balloon in here is a model of the one used on the day...
...there is a strong possibility something may be concealed inside it.
Something our absconder was desperate to retrieve before making a hasty getaway.
But, but the balloon's out of reach toute proche !
Hence why he resorted to a projectile. Namely...the chaussure.
Most probably, Drebber intended to tear a hole in the envelope by assailing it with the chaussure.
However, his efforts were thwarted when the chaussure itself became a prisoner of those lofty heights.
Oh dear... We desperately need to examine that balloon.
If only there were some way we could see inside...
You may recall that I found this in the room earlier, which I believe offers a solution.
To reach the intended destination, what better tool than this corde ?
To reach the intended destination, what better tool than this corde ?

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Mr Naruhodo... Would you care to explain that?
Oh, it's gone over your head, Mr Sholmes? Obviously, I was thinking of using it to examine the balloon.
On the contrary, nothing has gone over my head but this rope. For it is clearly the superior idea.
(Really? Throwing the rope to catch the balloon and tug it back down?)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: So...shall we?
Your curiosity is deeply stirred no doubt, my dear fellows.
What is it that Enoch Drebber has hidden inside that balloon...?
Indeed it is. A waxwork head inside a metal mask.
A mask that is shut tight and fastened with a strong and quite impenetrable lock.
Just a moment... This...this is the head of a waxwork model?
Does that mean...? Oh goodness!
I see you've joined the dots, Miss Susato. Excellent.
Ah! (Of course! A headless waxwork model!)
The case of the abducted Madame Tusspells model that you'd ‘largely’ solved...
It was only the head of the killer that was still missing!
But I believe Madame Tusspells will now have to settle her sizeable account with me.
This, as you have now surmised, is the head of the infamous Démon Assassin.
But why is it here?
...This conclusively confirms my suspicions.
The man responsible for stealing the Démon Assassin from Madame Tusspells...
...and returning it – sans tête – earlier today...was none other than Enoch Drebber!
(Démon Assassin Harebrayne's case and the waxwork abduction are...)
(They're inextricably linked! By Enoch Drebber's workshop!)
The waxwork head has been entered into the Court Record.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Well...it appears our logical pleasure cruise has come to an end, my dear fellows.
All that remains is... Yes, to speak with the architect of this adventure.
You mean...Mr Drebber?
As it seems quite impossible that he escaped via one of the skylights...
...obviously the man must still be here in the room.
And his location should be abundantly clear...
...if you simply reflect on the journey we've made together during this deduction.
(Enoch Drebber is right here, somewhere in this room?)
So, Mr Naruhodo, will you do the honours?

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Yes, plans and accounting ledgers...
Almost as if somebody was in a hurry to empty the contents of the safe, in fact.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Personally, I still think he might have escaped via one of those skylights.
I'm afraid your opinion might put you at loggerheads with the great detective.
...sometimes a man must stand up for what he believes in and fight.
Oh! ...Well in that case, I'll leave you to it!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: So...Mr Naruhodo.
I think perhaps it's time we ended this game of hide-and-seek, don't you?
Let's see... The combination was one...
I knew that! (Alright then. Here goes...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I think we have a fairly good idea of what's been going on here now.
But what about the two incidents you've evidently been involved in recently?
Professor Harebrayne's instantaneous kinesis experiment at the Great Exhibition...
...and the waxwork model you stole, which this head belongs to.
That's no ordinary head, you know. That's the head...of the Professor.
Clad in a mask with a lock so strong, I'm unable to open it safely to reveal the killer's identity.
I've been considering carrying it around as...protection. After all–
What's going on here, Gregson?
I'm sure you're aware that I have sole jurisdiction to investigate here.
Ah, um... Yes, well...
(Dr Sithe again. So the Forensic Investigation Team are here...)
And you know full well this engineer is a key witness.
If Lord Stronghart knew of this, you'd be finished.
You lot. Leave at once.
My dear madam, there's no need for such a threatening tone, I assure you.
After all, that's no way to greet an old acquaintance, is it, Dr Sithe?
(Mr Sholmes knows Dr Sithe?)
If it's protecting the machine next door that's causing such a sour expression on your face, you are quite misguided.
It's really nothing more than a shell, you–
But of course. We'll show ourselves the door. ...I see you haven't softened at all.
It would appear that our delightfully entertaining investigations have run their course for today.
But, but Mr Sholmes...!
Let us leave this place in the doctor's capable hands.
I said get out! Now! All of you!
Your presence here is not required either, Gregson.
...we'd never have found this place. And the whole workshop would've been blown to bits.
There was a time bomb set in here that this lot disarmed.
...! Somethin' given you a chuckle, has it, Drebber?
Ah, so sorry. Didn't mean to offend. You're quite right of course.
You did disarm the time bomb, didn't you?
Yes... You did disarm that one.
Eh? Wot are you...?
‘That’ one? Ya, ya mean...?
Of the enormous explosion that ripped through the experimentation stage at the Great Exhibition.
Professor Harebrayne's invention and all its secrets...were blown away forever.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: À présent, professeur... We really need you to remain calm in the courtroom today.
Gregson, mon cher ami, why the grim expression at this delightfully early hour?
The killer's autopsy report has been entered into the Court Record.
Moi, I don't know what to say! Merci, inspecteur !
Oui. We expect the prosecution to summon him as a witness.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: L'accusation believes today's proceedings will see the complexity of this case rise considerably.
Mais il souffre toujours d'amnésie...so there's really nothing we can do at the moment.
...who have been chosen at random to represent the will of the people in this courtroom today...
Naturellement, Votre Honneur. I'm sure we all understand the importance of doing our civic duty.
Ces charlatans de faussaires should feel the wrath of God, if you ask me!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Avant de commencer, Votre Honneur, there is a report I must read to the court.
The post-explosion photograph has been entered into the Court Record.
...the protection afforded to the machine by the Special Dispensation for Scientific Equipment Act a été révoquée.
The accused accepts responsibility for his part in the events that transpired.
He acknowledges that Mr Asman died as a result of the accident caused by his machine's malfunction.
So what exactly were these two men up to behind the defendant's back?!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Oui, why do I feel as though I've seen it somewhere before...?
Votre dossier indique that you are currently being investigated in connection with another case.
Oui, I constructed it. In precise accordance with the blueprints. But that's all.
Then the court would be very interested to hear your thoughts about the machine, j'en suis certain.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: All the spectators saw the birdcage appear above their heads and then crash headfirst into the Crystal Tower.

Yes, you might say that.

Malheureusement pour vous, the machine has been blown to kingdom come.
So there's really nothing left to explore...is there?
It appears that the kinesis machine was fitted with a timed explosive device of some kind.
And there's nothing left of that device either. Not a single shred of evidence remaining...I hear.

en_pages.text: La démonstration aurait pu être une supercherie, if there was somebody who looked sufficiently like the victim.
So it can't have been orchestrated using someone who looked identical to Mr Asman then.
(Just that the idea of someone who looked identical to the victim is playing on my mind...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: According to the many witness reports from those there at the time, yes.
Hm...unlikely. I rarely leave my workshop.
Yet another of your unique inventions was found at the scene.
Well...it was the unveiling of a machine I'd laboured over for many months.
I believe the victim's neck was broken from the headlong fall, wasn't it?
Even an infernal recluse like me reads the newspapers, you know.
According to the reports, two injuries were apparent on the victim's body.
Oui, he'd been stabbed in the chest by a screwdriver believed to belong to the defendant...
...and he had broken vertebrae as a result of a fall from a considerable height.
... Exact. My learned friend has been doing his research, it seems.
Forensic science is not yet at a level where such things can be determined.
What we do know is that the victim died having sustained both injuries at some point during the experiment.
And since he was found in the birdcage with his neck broken...
...It's obvious that he fell from a considerable height.
(Hm... I suppose that's hard to deny...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Well, before the demonstration began, the victim was alive on stage in front of the audience.
Yes...there are lots of witnesses who saw Mr Asman on the experimentation stage, that's true.
And the victim's neck broke as a result of an impact following a fall.
Logically, therefore, the victim must have fallen from somewhere.
The balloon that exploded was at an altitude of sixty feet. The point of impact on the tower was thirty feet up.
That difference of thirty feet is therefore the total distance the birdcage fell.
And there's no other location from which the cage could have fallen that distance if it didn't drop out of the sky.
...the victim himself must have been beamed from the stage into the sky above the Crystal Tower.
Dear me, every time I hear it explained, it sounds increasingly plausible.
It's all very well thought out.
The birdcage plummeting thirty feet through the air, I mean.

en_pages.text: Not in the slightest.
As I've said a number of times, I'm an engineer. My job is to manufacture according to the blueprints I'm given.
I would be inviting manifold problems if I foolishly allowed my brain to digest the ideas behind them.
I could be accused of stealing those ideas, for example.
But how is it possible to construct a machine without really understanding the principles it relies on?
Well, you're practising law without really understanding the principles it relies on, aren't you?
The point is, the experiment resulted in instantaneous kinesis taking place. As such, the science must be sound.
Yes. And really, experimental results are all that matters when it comes to proving a hypothesis.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: What do you think, Mr Naruhodo?
Well, now that the machine has been completely destroyed by yesterday's explosion...
...it's going to be impossible to argue its authenticity one way or the other.
But if we're unable to establish that it was a piece of stage trickery rather than genuine science...
...we will have no grounds on which to demonstrate Professor Harebrayne's innocence.
Both Mr Asman and this man in the stand tricked the professor and used him.
They took advantage of his naivety and his unbending belief in his work...and I won't let them get away with it!
(And seeing as the professor is an old friend of Lord van Zieks...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: We've examined the birdcage that crashed into the Crystal Tower ourselves.
Following the explosion, it fell some thirty feet into the glass of the Crystal Tower.
That level of damage is to be expected, surely.
I agree. The damage itself is entirely understandable.
...is the location of that damage.
All the breakages in the wood are at the base of the birdcage, not the top!
What are you saying?!
That's the opposite of where they should be!
That's right, My Lord.
The birdcage that was at the scene is damaged at its base.
So we have reports of the birdcage falling headlong into the Crystal Tower, yet the damage is at the bottom.
...that there were two birdcages in play that day, which were at some point switched!
Switched during what wasn't a scientific experiment at all...but an elaborate piece of stage trickery!
Good gracious! Explain yourself, witness!
If we examine the facts, there's only one logical conclusion we can draw.
The damage on the base of the birdcage clearly indicates that it crashed tailfirst into the tower.
But multiple witness reports claim it fell headfirst!
The birdcage materialised in the sky next to a balloon flying over the stage, following a spontaneous explosion.
It then proceeded to fall some thirty feet into the Crystal Tower in the ensuing deflagration.
Witness reports amid such chaos...are notoriously unreliable.
He plummeted thirty feet inside a heavy, wooden cage.
However he fell, it would be unsurprising to find one or two of his vertebrae crushed.
......... Kuh kuh kuh kuh kuh...
A riveting scientific analysis of events from the prosecution there.
Though to be even more rigorous, you would have to say it was only one vertebra, actually.
This witness is clearly a swindler, and one who deceived a personal friend of his.
‘If you're going to establish this deception, do it right.’
Ah yes, and there's one more point the defence appears to have forgotten.
It obviously wasn't a trick...as a certain truth very plainly demonstrates.
It seems to me that the cross-examination had better continue until we resolve this matter.
Mr Drebber, you will amend your testimony with details of this ‘truth’.
Of course. We must treat the matter scientifically, after all.
(Agh, I nearly had him there...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: The place I'm referring to...is here!
Which is exactly the point, My Lord. Yes, the birdcage was in the machine on the stage.
But what we must also consider, is the height of the stage itself.
Go on, Counsel.
It turns out that the experimentation stage was built at a considerable height above ground level.
If you look at the diagram, in fact...
...you'll see it's at about the same height above the ground as the balloon was above the crash site.
When the experiment got underway, the machine and the birdcage were engulfed in steam.
At that moment, the floor of the stage gave way and, if we assume there to be a void underneath...
...this birdcage and the one seen by the audience would have fallen almost exactly the same distance!
Once again, My Lord...
...this all points to the fact that there was not one birdcage, but two!
My learned friend...has no evidence that the stage had such a contrivance in its design!
Someone is responsible for the criminal destruction of the kinesis machine itself, it's true.
However, the stage still stands.
And take a moment to look at the photographic print of the scene following yesterday's explosion.
Good Lord! The metal grille that formed the floor of the machine is undone!
Yes, most likely blown open by the force of the explosion that destroyed the rest of the machine.
The defence calls for the space below the stage to be investigated...immediately!
Which means that it was you who built the two birdcages that were used to carry out this deception.
Whether Professor Harebrayne's hypothesis is sound or not makes no difference.
Because it's the construction of this machine that matters. A machine designed to take Mr Asman's life...
...and lay the blame firmly at the professor's door. Something that could only have been carried out...
...by you, Mr Enoch Drebber!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: If my learned friend has reached the end of his wild assertions...
...the prosecution would like to crush the defence's argument slowly...but surely.
...on two counts.
...before and after the experiment, this witness went nowhere near the kinesis machine.
Every relevant member of staff from the exhibition has attested to that.
And I believe members of Scotland Yard have also been on watch duty at every public experiment.
In other words, Mr Drebber had no opportunity to switch the alleged pair of birdcages.
But I've already explained why he wouldn't have needed to!
The nonsense with the crossbow? That doesn't bolster your case at all.
The man who disappeared from the stage and the man who crashed into the tower are one and the same.
The Forensic Investigation Team's report is unequivocal on that point!
Why would this man have wanted to take the victim's life? He had no reason to do so.
I have here a contract provided by the witness.
What contract is this, Lord van Zieks?
The contract into which Mr Drebber entered with the victim, Mr Asman. It reads:
‘Mr Drebber is to receive thirty percent of all remunerations from government grants or other income.’
Thirty percent? Certainly very favourable contractual conditions.
But there was one very important provision bolted onto that clause.
‘Mr Drebber may only uphold this right on condition that both contracting parties are alive.’
In other words, if either of us were to die, the contract would become null and void.
So you see, I had nothing to gain from Mr Asman's death. The diametric opposite, in fact.
Need I say more? The witness had neither an opportunity nor a reason to commit the alleged crime.
In short, the possibility of Mr Drebber having done as you suggest...is nil.
Hm... It seems the defence's assertion was somewhat wide of the mark.
Lord van Zieks...you will submit the contract as evidence, please.
Drebber's contract has been entered into the Court Record.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: (If Drebber had no opportunity to switch the birdcage under the stage with the one in the Crystal Tower...)
(...he couldn't have done it. And in any case, I have no idea what his motive might have been!)
...that still holds true, however.
There were two birdcages. The prosecution is unable to deny that.
And I've no doubt there are other aspects of your assertion that are undeniable truths, too!
Well, I must say I'm a little surprised.
I came here to testify about the machine I built, and instead my reputation is defiled.
But the prosecution's counter has set the record straight, I think.
It's impossible that I'm the culprit.
At the beginning of this trial, we believed that there was only one birdcage.
In other words, there was more to the demonstration than we realised at first.
I think it's abundantly clear that the same applies to the culprit.
...was constructed and set up in its entirety by you, Mr Drebber.
Therefore it's inconceivable that you had no hand in the events that transpired.
So if circumstances mean it's impossible that you could have carried out the crime yourself...
...it points to the fact that someone else was involved.
Someone else? Counsel, are you suggesting...?
Yes, My Lord! Mr Drebber had an accomplice!
An accomplice now? Well then, I presume...
...you're prepared for what's to come?
Now that you're accusing not only this witness, but someone else...of the most serious of crimes.
The prosecution will demand an equally serious punishment for your slander!
Do you intend to pursue this course, and formally accuse another party of involvement in this matter?
(At the moment, this is little more than a hunch on my part.)
(I don't know for sure if Drebber had an accomplice, or even if he really is the culprit here...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Someone intimately related to the crime, My Lord...and someone you surely wouldn't say you don't know!
Yes, thank you, I am aware of the person, obviously. But on what basis do you claim felonious involvement?
You surely wouldn't say you don't know...would you?
I'm sure you simply slipped and pointed to the wrong person, didn't you?
No ‘slip-ups’ this time, please, Counsel.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: What's wrong, my Nipponese friend?
Surely fear doesn't bind your tongue now. It's a little late for that.
(After all, naming her in this capacity is definitely going to make waves. ...A lot of waves.)
(I could very well turn every single person in this courtroom against me.)
I'm sure it will be alright, Mr Naruhodo.
...Thank you, Miss Susato.
The enemy always appears larger than life. But you'll appear exactly the same to the enemy!
...Alright then, here goes...
You've kept us waiting long enough. Your answer, Counsel...now.
The person who colluded with Mr Drebber in order to carry out this wicked crime...
...is Scotland Yard's coroner, Dr Courtney Sithe!
What, what the blazes are you talking about? Dr Sithe?
The head of the Forensic Investigation Team, and the coroner who conducted the autopsy on the victim?!
We know there were two birdcages. So who could have carried out the switch to complete the illusion?
The ‘accident’ happened in front of a huge crowd of spectators, and the area was immediately sealed off.
Then everyone, police officers included, were banished to make way for the Forensic Investigation Team.
When else could the switch have occurred? It can only have been in that team's presence.
It's essential that the court determines exactly what happened following the incident.
The defence demands that Dr Sithe be summoned to the witness stand at once to testify!
Standing up there, dragging the Yard's name through the mud!
I, I didn't mean to...
I know the woman veeery well. There's no better dead room worker out there!
How dare you call her a criminal?!
My learned friend's imagination appears to be wilder than the East End at night.
But the recklessness of your accusation aside, there's another grave problem with your argument.
Who do you claim acted as the victim's doppelgänger?
Hmmm... Certainly, if the ‘birdcage’ containing the body of the victim was exchanged for another...
...that cage must also have contained a body.
...no missing persons or accidental deaths of anyone even remotely resembling the victim have been reported.
Which means there was no one, dead or alive, who could have fulfilled the role of a body double for Mr Asman.
(If my argument is that there were two birdcages, then there must also have been one person inside each!)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: This person is the most likely candidate I can think of... wouldn't you agree?
Even you're turning your back on me, Miss Susato? I must be really wide of the mark!
...You have a head. Try using it.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Oh really. And when can the court expect an explanation?
Then you can take your leave of us until then.
People who procrastinate lose everything in the end, Mr Naruhodo.
We can discuss that later. But for now, you ought to consider what you can do, not what you can't.
Alright, yes. I'll think again...

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: We know that the victim, Mr Asman, was in the birdcage that was situated inside the kinesis machine on stage.
And therefore he couldn't have been inside the second birdcage. Instead, that contained something else...
What's been described as a ‘body double’, which is what fell from the sky and crashed into the Crystal Tower.
Yes, Counsel, according to your somewhat elaborate version of events.
And that ‘body double’ inside the second birdcage was in fact...
It's alright, Mr Naruhodo. You're ready for this.
Just steel yourself...and come out with it!
...Thank you, Miss Susato! I needed that.
As I was saying...the ‘body double’ inside the second birdcage was...
Open your eyes and look into mine, my Nipponese friend.
...what are you playing at?
(Stand firm now, Ryunosuke! This is the time to show your Japanese spirit!)
As the court will observe...this is a waxwork model.
A model, in fact, of an infamous London murderer from ten years ago: the Professor!
You started by indicting the leader of the Forensic Investigation Team as an accomplice in this crime.
And now you've moved on to indicting waxworks?
...Yes! That's about the size of it.
But why? And why THIS waxwork?
It looks nothing like the victim. In fact, it could hardly resemble him less!
If you want to know why...
...ask Mr Drebber.
Just days before Professor Harebrayne performed his public demonstration...
...Mr Drebber abducted this model from Madame Tusspells.
Did, did you say...abducted?!
Then the timing...
Is this true, Mr Drebber?
At first I couldn't see why Mr Drebber would have stolen the waxwork and then given it back again.
But now, the reason is clear.
He took it so that he could put it inside the second birdcage...as a body double for Mr Asman!
Are you hearing this, ladies and gentlemen of the jury? Are you hearing the defence's astonishing proposal?
That the witness fabricated this vast machine with the intention of deceiving some wretched scientist.
That he did so in collusion with the country's finest coroner, on a public stage in front of a vast audience.
And that, to effect the deception, he used a waxwork model that in no way resembles the victim.
Are we really to believe this far-fetched tale? What do you decide?
Yes, if you put it like that, of course it sounds implausible!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I need to speak, if you please.
Go ahead, Mr Foreman.
Myself and my colleagues have reached an agreement.
Very good. In that case...
...ladies and gentlemen of the jury, you will state your leanings for the court to hear now!
So, as indicated by the foreman, the jury has reached a consensus.
We shall get through this, Mr Naruhodo, as we always do.
And uncover some new truths along the way, I'm quite sure.
I'm going to have to appeal to the jurors as usual, and see if I can persuade them to change their minds!
The defence will now embark on a summation examination.
Are you and your fellows ready to proceed, Mr Foreman?
We are, My Lord.
In that case, I ask you now to state clearly for all present to hear...
...the grounds on which each of you has decided that the defendant is guilty of the crime of which he is charged.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I've known that woman for years! She'd never be an accomplice to anything!
It's utter nonsense to think those two would ever be conniving with one another.
Oh dear, this is most troubling... But surely the waxwork the man stole is nothing to do with the coroner, is it?
I have had my own problems with members of the police. I do not trust them much...
I've seen no rigorous proof that this waxwork was ever inside the birdcage. It's conjecture!
Accusin' someone without right evidences? Ee's not a proper job, is ee? I won't 'ave it!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: ...it seems the introduction of this waxwork model to the proceedings has polarised opinion.
Given that its face is obscured and its build in no way resembles that of the victim...
...I can only applaud my learned friend's temerity at suggesting it as Mr Asman's body double.
(Yes, the applause is deafening. ...And yes, I know it seems extraordinary.)
(That's why I have a strong feeling it's actually a greater clue than anyone yet realises...)
What are you thinking, Mr Naruhodo?
...but I feel as though there's a specific reason why it was used. Why it had to be this model.
Really? A reason why nothing else would do, you mean?
Yes. And I'm convinced...
...it's something far more significant than whether or not the model looked like the victim.
Well...if that's the case...
...we must prevent the trial from ending prematurely at all costs!
(I have to find a way out of this...!)
If you are ready, Counsel, you may proceed with the summation examination.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Parfaitement, « Oh. » That woman is at the forefront of this country's fight against crime.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Mon Dieu, but it would be delightfully romantic if they were somehow to have a mutual interest in the waxwork.
Ou peut-être between the defendant and the handsome prosecutor just there.
(Cette femme...may be more astute than I've been giving her credit for.)
... alors peut-être demonstrating some connection between the waxwork and Dr Sithe would be enough...

... cela signifierait it must have crashed into the Crystal Tower.

en_pages.text: Oui, it's a piece of broken glass that we found inside the jacket on the waxwork.
Much like the special glass that was developed for the construction of the Crystal Tower.

... lorsque le raisonnement est rigoureux, it's fair to say colour shouldn't come into it.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Oui, science is where you should direct your words of gratitude.

... Peut-être it's akin to fortune-telling with flower petals like people do back home?
Could you non at least wait until we've had more time to find the truth avant de sceller la culpabilité de l'accusé ?

en_pages.text: I presume that you heard what juror number six said in his statement?

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: La preuve that clearly links Dr Sithe to the mass murderer known as the Professor!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I said before that the court could not overlook your claim of evidence.
But it seems to me that overlooking it would have been the more preferable choice by some margin.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Et supposez-vous...there's some unsavoury relationship between those events?
There's no doubt in my mind that le Démon Assassin case...
Parfaitement d'accord. We can't let thc'est trial come to an end now.
Not while there's thc'est cloud of suspicion hanging over the Yard's de tout le Yard.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: You've pointed out that it's wrong to make an accusation without evidence.
But the accusation that the waxwork model was inside the second birdcage on the day in question...

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Mais, mais, Votre Honneur, attendez ! The defence is still in the process of establishing its argument...
En conséquence, I shall be requesting the final decisions of the members of the jury.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Parfaitement. My dear Daley will be ravenous by the time I'm home.
Eh bien pour commencer, perhaps you could listen to what's being said here in the courtroom?
...And perhaps if what you set before the jurors was more appetising, vous captiveriez mieux leur attention.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Ai-je observé de curieuses réactions, is that what you're asking?

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Une leçon...de vie. There may well be more to people than meets the eye.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: ...used as a ‘body double’ for the victim in this quite extraordinary case...
Je dois dire qu' it's extremely hard to believe the assertion could possibly be true.
Toutefois, it would appear that it does at least warrant further investigation.
It's the waxwork of the Professor that links Mr Drebber and Dr Sithe.
If the court is to delve deeper into the alleged involvement of the waxwork in this case...
...then the prosecution calls for the owner of the model to be summoned à la barre des témoins.
(...that Lord van Zieks would object to this whole line of enquiry...)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: But who knew the monster would come knocking at your door? Toutes mes plus sincères condoléances ! Ah ha ha ha ha ha !
It seems that everybody in the trial has a link to the case somehow.
And I've...accused you of being complicit in what happened.
Lord van Zieks won't be summoning me as a witness.
Lord Stronghart has forbidden it.
The Pandora's box you were warned about...is the Professor case.
But please don't make the mistake of thinking you'll get any information about it out of me.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: So...good day to you.
...the meaning will become all too apparent, whether you'd like it to or not.
Now then, I believe it's almost time.
I must make my way back to the public gallery. The edge of my seat awaits!
(I think maybe you're enjoying yourself a little too much...)
Ah yes, one word of warning before I go:
If, in the course of the trial this afternoon, you perceive even a shadow of doubt about the truth...
...don't let it out of your sight. Pursue it like a dog with a bone.
To the bitter end, you understand. Do not falter, whatever may come to pass.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: (What did that warning from Mr Sholmes really mean, I wonder?)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: (That's the key to the link between these otherwise unrelated individuals.)

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: And the proprietress of the Madame Tusspells Museum of Waxwork.
Pour l'instant, that is no more than conjecture proposed by the defence.
I don't know what face you've carved onto your fancy figure beneath that mask...
The family Tusspells has always prided itself on sculpting its models à la perfection.
There is a well known legend about the Tusspells waxworks from the time of the French Revolution.
We Tusspells will stop at nothing to obtain a faithful replica of our subjects.
It is the only way to obtain a truly lifelike representation of the subject.
Do, do you mean to say...que sous ce masque... ?
The killer...emerging from his own grave... It is a sight to behold. You should come.
I think, madame, it would be beneficial to hear your formal testimony on this matter.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Oui. I will do all that is necessary to achieve the true resemblance my family is celebrated for.
Naturellement, I was aware at the time that his identity was a secret.
The scene it depicts was the subject of many rumours in London ten years ago.
The ten-year-old article has been entered into the Court Record.
That is why I have reproduced the scene as carefully as possible in my museum.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Une vieille histoire vieille de dix ans...but one that no Londoner would ever forget.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: The scream finally found its way from the mouth of the young witness, qui prit ses jambes à son cou.
The, the corpse climbed out...of his own grave...?
Oui. The special exhibit was modelled on that very illustration.
Ah, I see that people from the East can be just as astute as the people of Europe.
After the criminal known as the Professor was killed by hanging...

en_pages.text: I have letters from imprisoned criminals all the time, you know.

en_pages.text: Mais, mais, Votre Honneur, attendez ! The defence is still in the process of establishing its argument...
En conséquence, I shall be requesting the final decisions of the members of the jury.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: I have here an autopsy report that was filed ten years ago now.
It confirms the death of the Professor following his execution at the gallows.
And...is that a problem?
I believe it is. Because your testimony, and a particular detail in the report...
...completely contradict one another.
Are you going to explain yourself, my Nipponese friend?
According to her testimony, Madame Tusspells was creating her wax impression just before dawn.
And at that time, rigor mortis had not yet set in.
Am I correct so far, madame?
As I said, the stiffening of the jaw is the first sign of rigor mortis, two to three hours after death.
But the man's chin was limp, so he cannot have been dead for a long time.
But on the other hand, if you look at Dr Sithe's report...
‘Death by hanging confirmed at midnight, 17th June.’
If the Professor indeed died at midnight that day...
...then by the time you were sculpting his face, rigor mortis would already have set in.
Oui! Yes, you are right. The chin, it would have been completely stiff.
In that case, there's only one possible conclusion:
The execution didn't actually take place at the stated time!
Ordaaar! Ordaaar! Counsel, this is beyond folly!
...but you also implicate members of staff at Barclay Prison where the execution took place!
My learned friend appears to have overlooked one very crucial fact.
The Professor died that night. Sans le moindre doute !
He did! Of course he did!
Yes, the Professor died that night.
What...what exactly are you suggesting did happen in that case?
(It's almost impossible to believe, but it would explain the link...)
(...between Dr Sithe, the Professor...and that one other person of interest!)
I have evidence that will explain exactly what I'm suggesting happened that night!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Erm...what have we here?
...I would strongly advise the defence to concentrate on what is happening right now in this courtroom.
Quite. The next time you present such a nonsensical article, Counsel...
...you may find that tonight is the night of your own execution!
(Great. I'm so looking forward to trying again now...)
I won't let anyone execute you, Mr Naruhodo! Not tonight!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Thank you for your attendance at such short notice... Dr Sithe.
I'm disappointed in you, Lord van Zieks.
You've completely betrayed the agreed policy of both Scotland Yard and the Prosecutor's Office.
Betrayal is not in my nature...as long as the truth isn't compromised.
If it is... If there's even a hint of wrongdoing...then no matter whom it concerns or disgruntles...
...I will pursue the matter to the bitter end. As would any prosecutor worth his salt.
...you took the victim's life by means of a machine that you constructed in your workshop.
...as the investigating coroner, you were the first on the scene to examine the victim's body.
...that you collaborated with each other and were both complicit in this crime.
At present, we have no definitive evidence. But we do have a very significant clue.
I'm talking, of course, about the waxwork!
This model of the killer known as the Professor...who was sentenced to death ten years ago.
I witnessed the man's execution with my own eyes. And officially pronounced him dead.
According to newspaper reports from the time, on the night following his execution...
...the killer came back to life.
Tsk! Don't waste my time!
...was you, Mr Drebber, wasn't it?
If what you saw in the graveyard that night ten years ago wasn't some chilling fiction, but reality...
...it would make you privy to a very great secret of Dr Sithe's.
A secret so profound, it could compel the coroner to agree to collaborate in your evil scheme, in fact.
Mr Drebber, tell the court!
Tell everyone the truth of what you saw that night in Lowgate Cemetery!
You can see the resemblance actually, can't you? With the man in Madame Tusspells, I mean.
Surely he's not going to claim that's really what he saw. Especially not after all these years.
He was a research student at the University of London, was he?
And a bit too clever for his own good, if you ask me...
What an interesting twist.
When at the time, not one person would take me seriously.
Yet now here we are, ten years later, and suddenly my story matters. And in a court of law, too.
Very well, then. If everyone so wishes.
Let's be frank. I'll tell you the truth of what happened that night...for what it's worth.
...your testimony, please. About the events of that night ten years ago.
You will tell the court exactly what you stumbled across in Lowgate Cemetery!
Yes of course. As you wish.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: Wait a minute! You're, you're claiming you didn't actually see the Professor now?!
Of course. You'd have to have a screw loose if you believed a corpse could come back from the dead.
But... So you're saying this article is...
...Not worth the paper it's printed on? I think that would describe it perfectly, yes.
...it nullifies your argument for why Mr Drebber and Dr Sithe would have been working together.
(So he's discrediting himself to cripple my argument?!)
Tell me, witness...
...you claim to have been in the cemetery on some... auxiliary business. Can you elaborate?
That's right. Graverobbing, to be precise.
As you know, Lowgate Cemetery is at the rear of Barclay Prison.
So among students at the university, it had a reputation for being haunted by the ghosts of condemned convicts.
G-Graverobbing, you say?!
Yes. Exhuming fresh corpses to sell is reasonably lucrative.
Of course, I never laid a finger on any valuables buried with the dead.
So you were one of the so-called Resurrectionists. A particularly unpleasant scourge on society.
Actually, my fellows and I went by another name: ‘The Repurposers’.
That, that is quite beyond the pale! You would invite divine retribution, sir!
Yes, well...I think I suffered retribution enough.
The Daily Circus...eventually unearthed my name and put it in print.
It caused me a great many headaches. In the end, I had to leave the university.
...That was the only paper with the bad grace to identify me unambiguously, I might add.
Out of interest, who drew the illustration for this article?
Ah yes, that was the reporter who exposed me. He sketched that right in front of me as I described the scene.
Obviously, as time ticked on, I bitterly regretted what I'd done.
Claiming to have seen something I never truly saw... Foolish. Very foolish.
Well, Counsel for the Defence...you may proceed to the cross-examination now.
At once, My Lord.

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: By ‘moonlighting’, you mean graverobbing, do you?
Surely you only need to look at the graveyard scene and my appearance to gauge the answer to that?
The lantern and spade...
But who on earth would want to buy a dead body?
In order to better understand the human body, the study of anatomy is crucial to medical science.
But there isn't a hospital in the world that has enough ‘specimens’ to work with.
...Though obviously they can't openly express an interest in obtaining more by dubious means.
As aspiring scientists, we young research students had no money to work with, as I'm sure you can imagine.
So we made surreptitious arrangements with a hospital via some of our medical student acquaintances.
We would never take anything of value from the graves. This was all for the furtherance of science, you see.
That's what we all told ourselves every time we stole into the graveyard at night, spade in hand.
You realise body-snatching is a serious crime.
If you were caught, you could expect the gravest of consequences.
We students were caught between the hammer and the anvil. We needed funds for research.
I'm quite speechless at the apparent levity with which you've revealed this abhorrent behaviour.
Well, if you wanted to know why I was there at Lowgate Cemetery, that's the reason.
But I never expected it to end the way it did. That...I regret to this day.

en_pages.text: The strange happening at Lowgate Cemetery...which you now deny.
Not entirely. I ran to fetch the police at the time, you know. I was shaking like a leaf.
But they didn't believe a word of it. In fact, I was very nearly arrested myself.
I started big, with the London News. But unsurprisingly, they didn't want to know, either.
In the end, though, it was reporters from the gossip rags, the gutter press, that came to get my story.
And it spread like the plague through the capital, as gossip-hungry Londoners lapped up the tale.
The story was in every single paper at the time, with the exception of some broadsheets.
And yet only two or three of them actually interviewed me personally.
Most of the accounts turned out to be very...interpretive ghost stories.
That particular journalist found me at my dormitory.
I don't know how, but he'd discovered my name.
So I recounted to him exactly what had happened that night.
And from your description, he drew this illustration?
Precisely. That's how I learnt that the condemned man was the infamous Professor.
Because the reporter told me so. I had no idea myself, you see.
Newspaper reporters are wont to snoop around in matters that don't concern them.
So the scene portrayed in the illustration is accurate, then?

en_pages.text: For some absurd reason, I was scared of the graveyard at night.
And as a result...only too willing to believe that nonsense about the dead coming back to life.
But you said you actually saw it.
I said what I'd seen in my mind's eye.
After all...resurrection is impossible, isn't it? You'd have to be unhinged to think otherwise.
...you have some evidence that proves I encountered the Professor that night?
(Is there any material evidence that could show he really did see the Professor?)
I know. I need to present it against that irritatingly backtracking statement of his!
The point is, that night was a pivotal moment in my life.

en_pages.text: A fellow graverobber? What are you talking about?
Well, I wasn't the only one busy in the cemetery that night, you know. Other body snatchers were at work.
Of course, when I saw one emerging from the hole he'd dug, my heart very nearly stopped.
So that's the terrifying sight I actually saw, you see.
You're claiming it was just another student on equally insalubrious business as yourself?
Many of the medical students would wear metal masks to protect them from bacteria during dissections.
Clearly the fellow was using such a mask to protect his anonymity...wouldn't you say?
But there's more to the story, isn't there? The article goes on to say:
‘In the next second, a gunshot rang out suddenly from behind.’
‘The bullet pierced the resurrected man's chest, whose breath then stilled once more.’
We might assume that the sexton discovered the miscreants at work, perhaps? And fired upon one of them.
If a gravedigger had shot someone in the cemetery, I think it might have been rather big news, My Lord.
Ah! Yes, well...
I can only assume it was an embellishment bolted on later by the reporter.
I can only assume it was an embellishment bolted on later by the reporter.
As I explained earlier, most of what the papers published about those events was fabricated nonsense.
The journalists had a great time fashioning it into a horrifying ghost story.
So...now you're saying there was no gunshot?
That's right, yes. I'm afraid so.
I mistakenly thought I'd seen a corpse coming back to life and then fled the scene. That's really all that happened.

en_pages.text: Yet Madame Tusspells has testified that you told her about both of those details.
Not true. I said nothing of the sort.
Without material evidence to the contrary, you have no grounds on which to question the witness's word.
...what exactly did Mr Drebber say about the blood that apparently spattered on him?
Alors, this is what he told me:
All of a sudden, he heard a very loud gunshot from behind his back.
The bullet hit the figure who was emerging from the tomb in the middle of the chest. In his heart.
Hm... One dreadful sight after another...
And since Monsieur Drebber was at that time facing towards the condemned man...
...the blood sprayed from the wound and spattered on his body. That is what he told me.
So...not an experience you would ever forget, is it?
Precisely. And I didn't forget it. Because, as I've already said...
...it never happened in the first place.
(He's clearly lying.)
We can't let him win, Mr Naruhodo!
So we mustn't overlook a single detail, no matter how small!

episode: Épisode 3 — Le retour de la grande âme égarée

en_pages.text: (Why would he suddenly change his tune and recant his claim?)
I wonder if perhaps...it's because his circumstances have changed now.
Well...if he admits to having seen the Professor emerging alive from his grave ten years ago...
...it will expose a secret in Dr Sithe's past that she would desperately want to hide.
Yes, of course!
...then if Drebber were to betray her, there would be no reason for her to continue to cooperate.
(In that case, there's only one way around it. I'll have to prove he really did see it.)
(Prove he really did see the Professor's corpse coming back from the dead as he originally claimed!)
Yes, Mr Naruhodo! Exactly!
