<E800 328><E563><E800 329><E003 10><E800 331><E145 126 77><E800 332><E117 126 35><E800 333><E003 20><E800 335><E041 126 92><E025 3>And that somebody...<E049><E003 2><E145 126 71><E144 126><E025 3><E238>was not me.<E023><PAGE>
<E800 336><E563><E800 337><E003 7><E001>

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Obviously, you knew the man then?
The Professor, I mean. Genshin Asogi.
Yes. I remember him well, in fact.
Would you mind...telling us what you know?
Well, having been condemned to death as he was, any contact I had with the man was short, obviously.
After that trial, which was carried out behind closed doors, attended only by elite members of the judiciary...
The outcome of the trial was set from the beginning, wasn't it?
It was a time of delicate diplomacy, when Britain and Japan were in the process of signing an important treaty.
As I was the chief warder, I oversaw his short stay in the cells until his final hour.
I remember being struck deeply by his noble character and incredible resilience.
He was a killer of many men, but he was always quiet and polite.
He was a gentleman, and a man of intellect.
In fact, I couldn't bring myself to believe what he'd done, so I asked him one day.
Those five members of the aristocracy whose lives were taken... Were you really responsible?
...I'm guilty of the unforgivable crime of ending another human's life, yes.
The following day, the closed trial took place. And the verdict was no surprise.
That night, when he was brought back to his cell...
...I saw something. Something...unusual.
Something unusual? What?
The last will and testament...of Genshin Asogi.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: As I said, it was on the night following his trial, after he'd been found guilty.
I was doing the rounds of the cells, and when I looked into Asogi's...
...I noticed that he seemed to have a sheet of paper in his hand.
Ah... (His last will and testament then, presumably.)
As soon as he noticed me, he hurriedly shoved it behind his back.
But...why did you find that so unusual?
Isn't it normal for a man to pen a will when he knows his death is nigh?
Yes, that's true. But there were special conditions to Asogi's incarceration, you see.
Well...even though he was held in a cell designed for condemned inmates...
...he was allowed to keep his personal effects with him, with one exception.
Really? He was allowed his things? (That is unusual, certainly.)
Of course, he'd been convicted of killing five members of the aristocracy...
...but at the same time he was a guest in our country from the Empire of Japan.
The powers that be were determined that his final days shouldn't be needlessly uncomfortable.
And what was the exception you mentioned...to the personal effects he was allowed?
That's the point. He wasn't permitted to have writing materials.
Specifically, no pens or paper.
So...he was prevented from leaving any written record of what had happened to him?
Yes, that was the long and the short of it. I've no idea where he obtained that paper.
As I said, he hid the paper behind his back and then he pleaded with me:
Please... Please, turn a blind eye. This...is my lifeline.
But...you know it's against the rules.
You're the only person who's seen. If you just agree to keep quiet...
Alright then. But what's on that paper?
This will is...the only weapon I have left now.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Alright then. But what's on that paper?
This will is...the only weapon I have left now.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: I was the only person who saw Asogi's will, but...
...But somehow it disappeared.
Which was actually an elaborate jailbreak!
They were all to be sent back to his family home in Japan, you see.
And you're saying that it wasn't anywhere to be found among his personal effects?
The will, I mean.
That's right. Though I didn't search through them myself.
But Governor Caidin was livid. He was screaming, ‘It cannae have disappeared completely!’
That...doesn't quite make sense though, does it?
Well, we'd understood that only Mr Vigil was aware of the will's existence.
In which case, how did the prison governor know to look for it?
Oh yes! You're right!
I really don't know how he knew.
But it certainly seemed as though he knew of the will's existence from the outset.
Only he didn't refer to it as a will. What he said was...
...the ‘Asogi Papers’.
Because...well...of what happened.
(Your dismissal...and the way you blocked it all from your memory...)
I'd forgotten all this until today. I don't suppose it's relevant to the case, though.
Well anyway, thank you very much for sharing it with us, Mr Vigil. We're very grateful.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Mr Vigil, would you mind casting your eyes over this?
Ugh... My head... It's, it's throbbing...
It's too soon, Mr Naruhodo! It's too much for him!

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Forgive me for asking, Mrs Vigil, but...have we met somewhere before? Quite recently, perhaps?
Pshaw! My dear fellow, what is your intention?
If you wish to invite the lady to tea, you must do so in a more gentlemanly fashion.
Ah! (I knew I recognised her!)
To have a man's fate in the palm of one's hand... Oh gosh! Oh golly! It sends shivers down my spine.
It must be very difficult for you as a lawyer. Being hard of hearing, I mean.
Oh dear! I'm so sorry! Don't worry if you can't hear. It was frippery really, nothing more.
(Now look what you've started, Mr Sholmes. Thank you very much.)

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Tell us about your husband, madam.
Mr Vigil – my Daley – is forty years of age.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Hm...an entirely unremarkable gentleman...by appearance at least.
We have a cordial relationship, and my husband's income is more than adequate so we live quite comfortably.
As it would appear. I need only look at you to know these things.
Your dress is the latest style, your hat clearly regularly groomed and your eyes are animated.
In short, you have no inkling as to why your husband might have disappeared. Correct?
That's right. He's a kind man with a strong sense of loyalty...and he rather dotes on me.
...that he has become embroiled in some incident or other.
Oh, that is exactly what I fear must have happened, Mr Sholmes! I'm quite beside myself!
My husband's employment is somewhat unusual, you see.
What exactly is your husband's line of work?
He's a warder at the prison.
(A guard? That is ‘somewhat unusual’.)

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: So...to the matter of your husband's disappearance. When did you realise he was missing?
...Please try not to laugh.
It was yesterday.
I'm sorry? Yesterday?
(That really is recent. Laughably so.)
The truth is my husband does at times have occasion to spend the night away for his work.
It's not at all out of the ordinary for him not to return home at night. But this is different!
For him not to make any contact for a whole day! That has certainly never happened before!
Oh, my dear Daley! Whatever can have happened?
My dear Mrs Vigil, please, calm yourself.
Now then...have you contacted the police?
Why, naturally! But sadly...
In truth, Mrs Vigil, I concur with the police.
However! Let us not be hasty!
Oh, thank you, Mr Sholmes!
And furthermore! Let me assure you!
A chance to solve the greatest problem known to man for another month has no bearing on my decision.
I seek only to put a sweet smile on another Londoner's face. ...That's really all there is to it.
You have my eternal gratitude! I shall pay any sum you care to mention!
(You seek only to put this suite's rent in your landlady's purse. THAT's all there is to it.)

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Governor Caidin, could I at least show you this?

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: If you'd just cast your eyes over this, Governor Caidin...
What's this then? You cannae pull the wool over my eyes, you good-fer-nothin' Japanese student!
That, that young jock from the forensics laboratory? That Mikotoba?
Yes! Exactly! Him!
Oh dear, perhaps I should have said something sooner...
I'm Yujin Mikotoba's daughter, Susato.
Jings! You're the young man's daughter?
And ya did'nae think to mention that afore?
I, I do apologise...
Aye, well, ye'd best take a seat then. Can I offer you a cup of tea, perhaps?
So then...what can I do for you, hen?
Well...we're currently investigating a case.
It's one of your warders, you see. He's gone missing.
That's right. It's surely been reported to you as well, being the prison governor.
I have'nae heard nothing of the sort. There's no missing persons in my prison!
(But...how can that be?)
It's Mr Daley Vigil, your chief warder...
That's right. His wife came to us and asked us to investigate his disappearance.
Would you be so kind as to tell us what you know, sir?
Aye... Aye, of course.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Aye, that he was.
Strong sense of responsibility and dedicated to the job, no doubt aboot it. He was a fine warder.
......... Sorry, did you say ‘was’?
Aye. He does'nae work here no more. He left the job.
There's a question. When was it aboot...? It cannae have been much less than...
...ten years ago now.
T-Ten years ago? He stopped working here ten years ago?!
Aye, as I mind it. D'you ken, I have'nae heard the fella's name in all that time.
But, but Mrs Vigil made no mention of it...
I think perhaps, Mr Naruhodo, that his wife simply doesn't know.
Governor Caidin, can you tell us what happened?
Why did Mr Vigil give up his job here?
That's...important, is it?
......... Yes, I believe it may be.
What are you thinking, Mr Naruhodo?
I can't help wondering...given that it was ten years ago...
(Which was exactly when the Professor was being held at this prison.)

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: So Mr Vigil actually resigned from the position of chief warder ten years ago, you're telling us?
What happened to make him leave the job?
In actual fact, he did'nae leave the job willingly. He had no choice in the matter.
You mean...he was dismissed?
It was...after a particular walk.
Aye, that's oor word for it in here. A walk to the gallows.
An, an execution...
It's the job of the chief warder to prepare the gallows tree and oversee any executions, you see.
Only...Vigil did something unthinkable on that last walk he was manning.
I'm sorry, but...I cannae reveal that information.
But why wouldn't Mrs Vigil know about it?
She appears to be under the impression that her husband still works here.
I would'nae ken anything aboot that, I'm afraid.
That last execution that Mr Vigil was responsible for overseeing...
Was it by any chance...the Professor's?
I'm sorry, I really am. But I'm no at liberty to answer that.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: My father came to Britain all those years ago in order to study forensic medicine.
But you seem to have been well acquainted.
The dead room, the prison and the cemetery have a lot to do wi' one another.
After all, they need fresh corpses for forensic research. D'you ken?
...Yes, I can imagine.
Your father worked in the laboratory just on the far side of the graveyard.
In the basement of St Synner's. It's still in use today.
St Synner's... (That's come up before, I'm sure...)
Yes, that's right. We've been there.
(For more ‘fresh’ material, I suppose...)
Aye, and we used to sit in here for hours and gab on aboot dissection and all sorts. Och, it takes me back.
Over a pot of tea and a plate of cuff biscuits, of course.
He was a good fella, your father. Reliable, and dead set on his work.
But I'm afraid...
...I'll never understand you Japanese.
(Because of Genshin Asogi, I suppose...)

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Well...if you have to wear something like that to prove who ye are...
...perhaps I should wear these handcuffs, eh?
I think maybe they're more of a sign of the people you catch than you yourself.
Aye, that's true. Ye've got me there, hen.
(They're not actually a sign of anything, are they?)

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: Well...how aboot that? A friend of Mikotoba turnin' up after all these years.
And his wee bairn, even.
My father speaks highly of you, sir.
D'you ken, I can see the resemblance now.
Aye, especially around your eyes. Ye look dead like him.

episode: Épisode 4 — Karma tordu et dernier coup d'archet

en_pages.text: How d'you come to ken aboot that, laddie?
There's no many folk even here in the prison who've heard o' those papers.
Ah...well... (I can't tell him Mr Vigil told me...)
I'm afraid our sources must remain confidential, sir.
We've been led to believe the papers are actually a last will and testament. Is that right?
The Professor's... Or rather, Genshin Asogi's...
Aye, that's right. ...You're well informed, Jimmy.
(Oh, is that the end of the silent treatment?)
But then after the convict's execution, it mysteriously vanished from his cell, didn't it?
Havers, no! You're off at half-cock there. I think you did'nae quite get your facts straight.
It was there in the cell, exactly where it should've been.
Oh... (Not what we heard elsewhere...)
Let me just have a wee holk aroond in here. I'm sure I can find it...
Aye, here ye are. See?
‘The Last Will and Testament of Genshin Asogi’... Written with a calligraphy brush...
Of course, I cannae read a word of those Japanese squiggles.
But I mind it says he leaves all his worldly possessions to his son back in his homeland.
Yes, that's correct. That's the gist of it.
So these...are the Asogi Papers?
Aye, of course they are! Papers written by Asogi, nae doubt aboot it.
There's no mystery here, laddie. That's your lot!
After all the stramash o' that slaister of an execution...
...we sent the man's possessions back to his clan in Japan... and that was the end of it!
I think we ought to make a record of this, Mr Naruhodo. Just in case.

en_pages.text: I dunno, do I? I'm just tellin' ya wot was written in the book!
Tobacco, tea, spices, medicines... Goods of all sorts flow into London by illegal channels from across the globe.
It's well known that they're disposed of at regular black markets that take place in the capital.
But the police are rarely able to locate them in time.
So Inspector Gregson was investigating one of those black markets?
It's been suggested that high-ranking government officials may be involved in black-market activity.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: I'm sure your superiors would be delighted that you're taking the initiative...
So I snuck into 'is office when no one else was about.
Cos if anyone at the Yard 'ad seen me goin' in there, they'd 'ave turfed me straight out on the street.
(This is sounding less and less like an investigation and more and more like something else...)
The prosecution understands that it was this very detective who discovered the notebook.
You got that right! Nuffin' gets past Inspector Lestrade and 'er trusty assistant, Chief Inspector Toby!
We found it 'idden in one of 'is desk drawers that 'ad a false bottom.
That's...impressive!
So then I went to 'ide meself where no one could find me so I could 'ave a butcher's at wot was written in it.
Cos if anyone at the Yard 'ad found me out, they'd 'ave turfed me straight out on the street.
I've given it in now though, ain't I? An' if it weren't for me, it wouldn't never 'ave been found!

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: That's the question, ain't it? But I'm just an apprentice, so...
And why didn't he inform Scotland Yard of his findings?
Yeah, that's wot I was askin' meself. Cos – ya know – I'm just an apprentice.
When it suits you, yes.
Anyway, the point is, somefin' went on at that club, no question.
You can't say that for certain though, surely?

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: I've read about these clubs that exist here in Britain.
As I understand it, they're places where well-to-do gentlemen socialise with friends and colleagues.
Don't imagine for a second that a foreign student like you would be admitted.
(Seriously, is your mirror cracked or something?)
Do we know for sure that the contraband dealings were definitely happening at a club called ‘The Grouse’?
...The police are currently looking for evidence... but haven't found anything definitive yet.
And I'm sorry to say that they probably won't.
What do you mean by that?
I mean that the place Inspector Gregson was secretly going to visit on 31st October...
...may not have been a gentleman's club at all.
...You're showing a very irreverent attitude towards our country's police force there, Counsel.
If it wasn't a gentleman's club...then what was it?
You think...it's a ship...?
I have the evidence to prove it here!
Let me see that.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: I'm suggesting that just one day before the inspector's body was discovered...
...there's a distinct possibility he wasn't even in the country!
This document is for passage to France. It does appear to have been officially authorised.
The day before the SS Grouse arrived at Dover...
...it docked on the northern coast of France for a night.
According to my father, who was on board...at the Port of Dunkirk.
What could possibly have taken the victim there?
Ha ha ha ha ha hah! I'm impressed, Ryunosuke Naruhodo!
I certainly didn't expect you to get your hands on that passport.
You mean...you knew about this?!
The prosecution's strategy for this trial has been laid down by the Crown prosecution office:
‘On the day before the incident, the victim was investigating contraband dealings at a London club.’
That's the outcome of Scotland Yard's investigations and the line the prosecution has been asked to follow.
...But personally, I don't agree.
I think the Prosecutor's Office is trying to hide something.
And now that you've expertly disproven their assertion... I intend to reveal what I believe that something to be.
...What are you playing at, Prosecutor Asogi?
A courtroom is a forum for the truth, My Lord.
Which is why it's my duty to present all the facts, without exception.
Let me guess... This was your intention from the outset, wasn't it?
The reason Inspector Gregson secretly made his way to the steamship docked in France on the day in question...
...was to carry out a mission...for the Reaper!
The, the Reaper?!
Order! Order! What on earth are you saying, Counsel?
The prosecution made an assertion in court yesterday:
Inspector Gregson was investigating the identity of the Reaper.
When he discovered the location of the man's secret hideout...he was killed.
As I'm sure everyone can imagine...by the Reaper's hand!
But in reality...the truth is the opposite of that.
Inspector Gregson wasn't investigating the Reaper at all.
He was in fact...acting FOR the Reaper!
So...you're saying the mission he was undertaking was...
Obviously...an assassination.
Barok van Zieks never carried out any of the actual killings.
Whenever the Reaper's victims lost their lives, he always had a cast-iron alibi.
Which tells us...that he must have had an accomplice.
And you claim...that was Inspector Gregson?
W...Wot the 'ell d'ya think yer sayin', eh?
My boss would never o' done nuffin' like that!
And yet...when you consider all the facts, it all makes perfect sense.
No! It, it can't be...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: But that's...Judge Jigoku!
Seishiro Jigoku... Certainly not an English name, you're right.
But that can't be right! I know Judge Jigoku! And I saw him the day before yesterday! Here in London!
So I know for a fact that the man hasn't been assassinated!
As I said...the Reaper failed.
Gregson missed his chance to kill his mark and returned to British shores.
But the Reaper wouldn't tolerate the mistake.
So he killed the inspector...personally.
The Reaper of course being the accused...Barok van Zieks!
It's...an undeniably logical argument.
(You planned for the trial to go this way all along, didn't you?)

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: In other words, it shows that Gregson was basically acting as the Reaper...
Not you an' all! That ain't the only explanation, is it?
'E could 'ave been investigatin' the Reaper in secret and that notebook said wot 'e found out!

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Ah! Then perhaps what it said on the passport document...
‘Permission for the applicant and one additional person to travel’. Could that additional person have been...?
Clearly the assassin, who was meant to take Seishiro Jigoku's life.
Gina! Can you confirm that?! Against the final entry that listed ‘Grouse’ and ‘Seishiro Jigoku’...
...what name was written?
Oh! Well...that's the only entry that didn't 'ave a name next to it, as it 'appens.
It, it just 'ad like a question mark or summat there, I think.
In other words, Gregson himself didn't know the identity of the assassin in that case.
But...Gregson was the one making the plans, was he not?
Oh...how infuriating!
(A nameless assassin...?)

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: I, I don't...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Of course...by you, Lord van Zieks.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Lord van Zieks!
Let me guess: is there something about the witness's last statement that troubles me?
Is that what you wish to ask?
Y-Yes... Exactly... You're very perceptive.
Whereas you...would appear not to be.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Ow ow ow ow ow!

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: K. Asogi, A. Shinn...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: That's right.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Very well, then.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Hm? Yes, of course. He burst in immediately without knocking.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: ......... Ha ha ha ha ha ha hah...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Lord Mael Stronghart...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: I beg your pardon?

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: ...open your eyes.
You must know deep down...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: I beg your pardon?

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: In other words...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: ...in the fella's cell where I said it would be!

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: It's curious...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: That's right.
Oh! You, you mean...
...Yes, that was it.

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Is that really what you saw?!
Well...yes, you're right...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: Im-Impossible! That can't be!
Everything that's happened...comes back to this will.
...is the key that will unlock the entire mystery!
My, my brother's last will and testament... Where did you find that?!
It was rolled up inside this.
I-Inside Karuma?!
That ultimate weapon Genshin Asogi obtained has lain undisturbed in the hilt of this sword all these years...
...just waiting for the right time to emerge...and reveal the truth!
The signature and seal certainly look official.
......... My God, it's true...
It's my brother's handwriting! There can be no mistake!
I forbid the contents of that document from being read out! Do you hear me? I strictly forbid it!
You can't do that, My Lord. This document could explain everything!
That document could literally destroy the meaning of justice in this country!
I demand that you hand it to me...AT ONCE!
Why? What are you trying to hide?
...that you already know what's written on this page?
Argh! W-What are you implying?!
Court is adjourned with immediate effect! Clear the courtroom!
Do that, My Lord...
...and you'll suffer a fatal blow as Lord Chief Justice.
I beg your pardon?
Forcibly ending a trial without good reason?
And not any trial. A closed trial by order of Her Majesty the Queen.
To defy the monarch's will is treason!
Lord Klint van Zieks really did pen a will that day...
It's exactly as the young Japanese man said!
Read it out! Now!
We have a right to hear what's in that will! A right...and a duty!
Well well, My Lord...
...it would rather appear as though proceedings aren't going to go quite as you'd hoped.
You... You fools...
Go ahead, Ryunosuke. Read it!
The prosecution...gives its full support!
Very well then...
No... For God's sake...

episode: Épisode 5 — La détermination de Hikari Yûno

en_pages.text: ‘As I watched my former mentor perish before my eyes at the jaws of the hound I commanded...’
‘...I realised that I had lost the last shred of decency within me...and sunk to the level of a wild beast.’
